title: SOC2 guerilla playbook - personal scratchpad
content:
Very rough scratchpad for me (Hannah) — treating this like a whiteboard I can destroy afterwards. Not a formal narrative; just thoughts + quick mappings + TODOs.

Goal: get minimum viable evidence and control narratives together so we can run a lightweight internal evidence-mapping strike team and reduce last-minute scrambles during audits.

Key constraints / assumptions:
- We want to avoid heavy infra changes if possible; prefer documentation + config + monitoring evidence first.
- Prioritize controls that auditors always ask for: access reviews, logging (create/delete/iam), change control, backup/restores, crypto key mgmt, incident response traces.
- Timeline: internal dry run in 4 weeks; external auditor kickoff in 10 weeks.

Quick control mapping (first pass)
- Access management (CCO-1): map to Okta groups + SCIM provisioning logs. Evidence: Okta group export, last-30-day SCIM events, invite flow screenshots. Hook: JIRA-SOC2-1987 for automated monthly export.
- Principle of least privilege (CCO-2): IAM policies review doc + list of service accounts with wide perms. Evidence: iam-policy-snapshot-2026-03-01, playbook for monthly access review. Owner: Rohan.
- Logging & monitoring (LOG-1): CloudTrail / Stackdriver / Datadog logs retention setting (90 days min). Evidence: retention config screenshot, sample CloudTrail event (create-instance + delete-bucket). Gap: S3 bucket for audit logs currently TTL 30d -> need to bump to 90d or archive to Glacier.
- Change management (CHG-1): GitHub PRs + deployment tags + release notes. Evidence: release tags for last 6 months + changelog. Action: add PR template that references jira ticket and test run id. Owner: Kaiya.
- Encryption & KMS (CRY-1): KMS key rotation policy + key access docs. Evidence: KMS policy export, last rotation timestamp, who has Decrypt/Encrypt. Gap: one legacy key in project "dev-legacy" has 3 principals with wide access.
- Backup & restore (BKR-1): nightly DB snapshots + restore test doc. Evidence: snapshot logs, sample restore runbook and successful test. TODO: schedule an ad-hoc restore drill this sprint.
- Incident response (IR-1): pager duty rotations + incident postmortem template. Evidence: recent postmortem (2025-11) + runbook link. Gap: playbook lacks verification steps for modeling data exfil.

Evidence shortlist (quick wins)
- Okta: last 30 days group membership export (csv)
- Cloud: CloudTrail sample event + retention screenshot
- Infra: IAM policy snapshot (json)
- GitHub: last 6 months release tags and one production deploy PR
- KMS: key policy export + rotation record
- Datadog: alert rule list + one recent alert timeline (linked graph)

Short scripts / helpers I want to build (scratch)
- small python to pull Okta group membership + write csv + upload to evidence bucket (s3://redwood-evidence-temp). Link to PR: infra/pr/1012 (WIP).
- terraform plan -> comment on PR with plan hash and checklist (auto link to jira). Helps CHG-1 evidence.

Unresolved questions / decisions to make
- How strict do we need MFA enforcement evidence to be for non-interactive service accounts? (ask security-architecture)
- Are we OK with 90-day log retention, or do auditors prefer 1 year for certain event types? (I think 90d common but sensitive ops ask for longer)
- Do we treat "Dedicated" infra accounts separately from Hosted? Need to document segregation clearly — map to two control narratives.

Proposed lightweight runbook for internal dry run (4 weeks)
Week 0: baseline collect (owners export their artifacts to /evidence/dryrun-2026-03)
Week 1: evidence triage meeting (30m) — assign missing pieces + owners
Week 2: fill gaps (scripts + screenshots) + write control narratives (one pager each)
Week 3: internal dry run: auditor-style walkthrough with two engineers playing auditor + vendor
Week 4: retrospective + final polish -> hand-off to audit manager

Control narrative skeleton (template)
- Control name + id
- What the control is trying to prevent (one sentence)
- Where this control is enforced (Okta / IAM / KMS / App) + owner
- Evidence list (files + links)
- How often we verify (monthly/quarterly)
- Known gaps + mitigation plan

Things I should call out to Slack #trust-ops (quick messages)
- "Heads up: I'm running a quick evidence sweep next week for SOC2 dry run. If you own IAM/KMS/GH releases please save exports to /evidence/dryrun-2026-03 by Tue 03/02."
- "Anyone with access to legacy dev-keys: let's audit principals and rotate/archive by 03/10."

Low-friction evidence hacks (not ideal but auditor-acceptable if explained)
- Export CSV snapshots of group membership with timestamp + sign-off from group owner (email thread).
- Annotated screenshots of console settings (include URL + timestamp + actor).
- Signed/dated runbook changes committed to a docs repo with commit hash (evidence of change control).

Possible risky shortcuts to avoid
- Fabricating sample events instead of real logs -> bad. Always prefer real events or annotate as simulated in explicit form.
- Using screenshots without making them reproducible (record the steps to reproduce).

Immediate TODOs (today)
- Create ticket JIRA-SOC2-2001: evidence bucket + ingest path for dryrun (Hannah)
- Ping security-architecture re: MFA for service accounts (message sent, awaiting reply)
- Run Okta group export (quick script) and put CSV in /evidence/dryrun-2026-03 (deadline 2026-02-23)
- Tag Rohan + Kaiya on JIRA-SOC2-1987 to confirm owners for IAM & CHG controls

Notes from last convo with auditor lead (Laura)
- They prefer documented, reproducible steps to get each piece of evidence.
- Screenshots ok but must be supplemented by exports or logs.
- They asked specifically to show "a recent access review" rather than a theoretical policy — so schedule one now.

Misc mental models (why this matters)
- Auditors want reproducibility and chain-of-custody for evidence. If we can provide scripts that extract artifacts reliably, that's gold.
- Emphasize people + process over big infra changes for this cycle; we can backlog larger hardening items to Q3.

End notes (scratch)
- Keep this doc ephemeral. After dry run, formalize narratives into Confluence and link here.
- If anything here becomes policy, move to product-security playbooks repo.

---

(Loose thought: run a "mini-audit" every quarter internally with rotating engineers. Make it blameless and fast.)
